segments.text:
- `go2.sh` prints this line first. 15823 is the process id of the shell that runs `go2.sh` [Ref1].
- The text in brackets is a hint for the operator. The command `kill -TERM -- -15823` sends the signal TERM (a request to stop) to every process of the process group 15823 [Ref8].
- The hint works only when `go2.sh` is the first process of its own process group. This was the case. The start command ran `go2.sh` through the tool `setsid`, which starts a program in a new process group [Ref11].
segments.heading: Start of the log

segments.text:
State at the start of `go2.sh`, printed by its function `state` [Ref1]. The text of this function is equal to the one in `go.sh`. Fields from left to right:
- `== start`: the label that the caller passes. `utc`: the time on the clock of CRB in UTC, from the command `date -u`. This line is 77 s later than the last state line in the log of `go.sh` [Ref5].
- `boot`: the boot id, read from the file `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`. It is the id that the log of `go.sh` shows [Ref5]. Before the first step `go2.sh` tests that it is the id of the boot in which 12 memory modules at 7200 MT/s were recorded.
- `MemTotal:`: the line `MemTotal` of the file `/proc/meminfo`. It is the usable memory that Linux reports, here 395392808 kB. Before the first step `go2.sh` requires at least 395000000 kB as the sign of 12 modules.
- `load`: the content of the file `/proc/loadavg`, five fields. The row of line 3 explains them. Here the 1-minute load average is 29.09.
- `users 0`: the number of lines that the tool `who` prints, one line per login. `marker absent`: the marker file does not exist.
- `processes per user:`: the tool `ps` prints the user name of every process of the machine, and the script counts equal names. The log holds these counts only. It does not name the processes.
segments.heading: State line `start`: the fields of every state line

segments.text:
State after the first wait and before step T72I1. The function `waitidle` of `go2.sh` reads `/proc/loadavg` every 5 s until the first number is below 1.0. After 180 readings (15 min) without success it stops the script [Ref1]. This wait took 205 s (22:23:35 to 22:27:00). The five fields of `load` [Ref4]:
- `0.95 36.39 38.17`: the load average over the last 1, 5 and 15 minutes. A load average is the number of tasks that are runnable or wait for disk input and output, averaged by Linux. `waitidle` tests the 1-minute value only.
- `1/1042`: 1 task is runnable at this moment, and 1042 tasks exist.
- `15940`: the process id of the newest process on the machine.
segments.heading: Step T72I1: wait for an idle machine, then one bwx12 process

segments.text:
Output of the last line of `rx.sh` for step T72I1 (first process of control I) [Ref2].
- `done`: the result folder. It holds `a6456.csv` (the rows that bwx12 printed), `env.txt`, `launches.txt` and `stderr.txt`. `rx.sh` started at 22:27:00. The process gets the arguments of `like.spec`, the argument line of part L [Ref9].
- `2`: the number of non-empty lines in `launches.txt`. They are one `launch` line and one `rc` line of the one process.
- `0`: the number of bytes in `stderr.txt`. So bwx12 wrote nothing to its error output.
- Between the two numbers `rx.sh` would print each `rc` line with an exit status other than 0. After the second number it would print the first 600 bytes of `stderr.txt`. Neither is present.

State after step T72I1. The step took 67 s (22:27:00 to 22:28:07). `go2.sh` prints this line only when `rx.sh` has returned status 0 and the function `rxok` has found exactly one `rc` line in `launches.txt`, with exit status 0 [Ref1]. 1-minute load average: 76.28.
State after the second wait and before step T72I2. This wait took 260 s (22:28:07 to 22:32:27). The 1-minute load average is 0.99, below the limit of 1.0.
segments.heading: Step T72I2: second wait, then one bwx12 process

segments.text: Step T72I2 (second process of control I, same arguments). The three lines have the same meaning as lines 4 to 6. `rx.sh` started at 22:32:27.
State after step T72I2, the last step. The step took 67 s (22:32:27 to 22:33:34). 1-minute load average: 70.15.

`go2.sh` prints the state once more, with the label `end`. The time is the same second as in line 12. Apart from the label, all fields are equal to line 12 except the newest process id (16549 against 16533).
- The process count of `root` is 1014 in line 2 and 1008 here. In the log of `go.sh` it is 985 to 1004 [Ref5]. The counts of the 7 other users are the same in every state line of the two logs.
- Insufficient data: which processes of `root` started or ended between the state lines. A list of the process names at each state line would resolve it.
segments.heading: End of the run

segments.text:
Last line that `go2.sh` prints. The script reaches it only when it did not stop before. It stops with a line `FAILED:` in four cases [Ref1]:
- a check at its start fails
- the marker file exists during a wait, or a wait reaches 15 min
- `rx.sh` returns a status other than 0
- `rxok` does not find exactly one `rc` line with status 0
After the line `FAILED:` the script prints one state line with the label `abort` and ends with status 1. The analysis scripts test for the line `ALLDONE` and for lines that start with `FAILED` [Ref6] [Ref7].
